chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad asked him, 'Zakat is obligatory upon you.' He replied, 'No, but we give extra (khums) like this.'

And he (peace be upon him) was asked about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'And know that whatever of anything you acquire as booty, one-fifth of it is for Allah and the Messenger and [for] the near relative and the orphans and the needy.'
It was said to him, 'Then to whom does that which is for Allah belong?' He said, 'It belongs to the Messenger.' And that which is for the Messenger, it belongs to the Imam.
It was said to him, 'What do you think if one category is more than another category, and one category is less than another category? How should we deal with it?'
He said, 'That is up to the Imam.'
'Do you see how the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) acted? He used to give according to what he saw fit; likewise the Imam.'
ai.seo_question: How is the khums distributed according to Shia jurisprudence based on the Quranic verse?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the theological hierarchy of Khums distribution, establishing that the divine share is effectively transferred to the Prophet and subsequently to the Imam, who holds exclusive authority over its allocation. It highlights the Imam's discretionary power (taqdir) to distribute the shares among the five categories—Prophet, Imam, Dhu al-Qurba, orphans, and poor—based on wisdom rather than fixed proportions, a principle rooted in the Prophet's own practice. This underscores the Imam's role as the rightful executor of divine wealth in Shia jurisprudence.
